html:
After the Soviet invasion of 1979, around five million Afghans fled their country, mostly to Pakistan and Iran. For years Afghans were the largest refugee population in the world.

War, bombing and the destruction of villages drove them out. In Pakistan, refugees lived in large camps around Peshawar and in the border lands among fellow Pashtuns (Afghan refugees in Pakistan). In Iran, most lived in cities and worked as labourers (Afghan refugees in Iran). Aid agencies such as the United Nations refugee agency fed and housed them.

The camps became bases for the mujahideen fighting the Soviets, and later religious schools there helped produce the Taliban. Many refugees went home after 1992 and again after 2001, but new waves left with each new war, and many never returned. The fall of Kabul in 2021 set off another flight, seen in the Kabul airlift.
sum: After the Soviet invasion of 1979, around five million Afghans fled their country, mostly to Pakistan and Iran. For years Afghans were the largest refugee population in the world.
